title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. In the sequence of notes on the 'équation des lacets' (the continuation of La Longue Marche), Grothendieck studies equations in a group scheme G(M), apparently GL of a rank-2 module M over a base S. Here ρ and σ are fixed sections, and ε_1(μ-1) is a unipotent element built from a scalar μ ∈ Γ E'_S. The previous page identified a scheme B'_0 with the scheme X_{ρ,σ} of triples (ξ, η, μ) satisfying equations (33)-(35). The next page shows the identification is u ↦ ([u,ρ], [u,σ], det u). A 'Scholie' then notes that X_{ρ,σ} inherits a group structure by transport of structure.

This page, part 1 (formula (81)). The transported group law is made explicit. If u ↔ (ξ, η, μ) and u' ↔ (ξ', η', μ'), then u'' = u'u corresponds to:
- μ'' = μμ';
- ξ'' = u'(ξ)ξ';
- η'' = u'(η)η'.
Here u'(x) = u' x u'^{-1}. This is the standard cocycle identity for commutators, [u'u, ρ] = u'[u,ρ]u'^{-1} · [u',ρ], together with multiplicativity of det.

This page, part 2 (section III, 'Étude de l'équation (suite)'). The equation (82) αρα^{-1} = βσβ^{-1} ε_1(μ-1) is written as (82 bis) [α,ρ] = [β,σ] ε_1(μ-1), in the commutator convention [x,y] = xyx^{-1}y^{-1}. Here α, β are sections of G(M) and μ is a scalar section. Let G_{ρ,σ} be the scheme of solutions (α, β, μ). Then (83), (α, β, μ) ↦ ([α,ρ], [β,σ], μ), is a morphism G_{ρ,σ} → X_{ρ,σ}. By the earlier theorems it is an epimorphism.

Next page. The morphism has a canonical 'diagonal' section u ↦ (u, u, det u) through B'_0. The general solution is (ua, ub, det u), with a ∈ T_ρ and b ∈ T_σ (centralizers). So G_{ρ,σ} is a torsor-like fibration over X_{ρ,σ} ≅ B'_0 with fibres T_ρ × T_σ.

Purpose. The goal is to describe the full solution scheme of a two-commutator ('lacets') equation by reducing it to the group scheme B'_0 and to the centralizers of ρ and σ.
errors: No mathematical errors: formula (81) is correct with u'(x) = u'xu'^{-1} and [u,ρ] = uρu^{-1}ρ^{-1}.
Minor notational mismatch: (82) has μ ∈ Γ E_S here, while elsewhere the notation is E' / E'_S.
On the next page, (86) writes u a^{-1} where the text says ua; harmless since a ranges over a group.

ideas.what: Transport of a group structure to the solution scheme X_{ρ,σ} via u ↦ ([u,ρ],[u,σ],det u), with the explicit law ξ'' = u'(ξ)ξ' (commutator cocycle identity)
ideas.modern_name: crossed-homomorphism / 1-cocycle identity for commutator maps; transport of structure

ideas.what: Fibring the solution scheme of [α,ρ] = [β,σ]ε_1(μ-1) over X_{ρ,σ} as an epimorphism with a diagonal section and centralizer fibres
ideas.modern_name: solution scheme as a torsor under centralizer group schemes T_ρ × T_σ; representation-variety-type computation
ideas.usually_credited_to: routine; general framework of group schemes (SGA 3)

deep.surprise_reason: Routine bookkeeping in a long computational study: an explicit group law via the commutator cocycle identity, and the structure of the solution scheme of a commutator equation fibred over a known scheme with centralizer fibres. Nothing here appears new or unexploited.
transcription_corrections: In (82) the scalar appears to be μ ∈ Γ E'_S (with a prime, as on the next page) rather than E_S; uncertain.
Γ 𝔊(M) is likely Γ G(M), the same group scheme G(M) as on the previous page.
The headline 'III) Étude de l'équation' carries '(Suite)' in the right margin.
